topic: Best medical therapy in peripheral arterial disease
usual_baseline: Antiplatelet use is often high but not universal (38.9–100%). High-dose statin optimisation is poor: 28% [2176], 29% [2509]. Lipid profiles are rarely checked (2.9–12.4%) [2729, 2799], HbA1c in 17.7–28.6%, and smoking cessation is documented in 13.9–40.5% [2729, 2441, 2015].
fix_that_works: Teaching plus a ward-round computer raised smoking cessation advice from 19% to 100% [2015]. An admission document prompting antiplatelet and statin review raised BMT on discharge from 40% to 80% [2176]. MDT education raised atorvastatin 80mg optimisation from 29% to 64% [2509]. Teaching and posters raised lipid profiles from 12.4% to 65.0% and gastroprotection from 35.3% to 66.7% [2799].
fix_that_fails: After teaching and posters, statin use stayed at 80% and HbA1c checks reached only 30.0% [2799]. After education and a handover proforma, 13% were still discharged on no secondary prevention (15% before), and statin initiation reached only 41% [2464]. BMT on admission stayed low (25%) [2176].
consultant_advice: Many vascular units audit BMT and most find the same gaps. A prompt built into the admission or handover document does better than teaching alone. More useful would be tracking high-intensity statin dose, smoking cessation referral and whether primary care continues therapy after discharge.
